title: MET CAL EXAM
topic: Altimetry calculations (true altitude, temperature/pressure corrections, flight levels)
notes: Transcribed from scanned tablet screenshots. 'selected_answer' is the option highlighted in yellow (or handwritten in the answer box for fill-in questions); it reflects the test-taker's choice, not a verified answer key. 'explanation' transcribes the handwritten calculations; Thai annotations are kept with English translations in brackets.

questions.question: An aircraft has to fly over a mountain ridge. The highest obstacle, indicated in the navigation chart, has an elevation of 10290 ft. The QNH, given by a meteorological station at an elevation of 5200 ft, is 1013 hPa. The OAT = ISA-20° C. Calculate the approximate indicated altitude, respectively flight level, to obtain a clearance of 2000 ft.
explanation: TRUE ALT = INDI ALT + (4/1000 x ISA Dev. x AAL)

questions.question: The crew is planning a flight across the Himalayas at FL400, which is above the tropopause. The QNH at the station located at 5000 ft is 1013 hPa. Forecasted temperature at FL400 is -50 °C. What would be the clearance above the peak of 29 029 ft.

An aircraft maintains a constant indicated altitude of 6500 ft from A (600 ft AMSL - QNH 1012 hPa) to B (930 ft AMSL - QNH 977 hPa). Assuming that the altimeter subscale setting remains unchanged at 1012 hPa, the height of the aircraft above the surface at B are:
(Barometric lapse rate: 27 ft / hPa)
A temperature of 10 °C below ISA is observed. What is the vertical distance between FL40 and FL70?
The average temperature of an air mass is ISA -12°C. Determine the vertical distance between FL80 and FL50...

What is the approximate true height of the aircraft above the airport considering the following data?
• OAT: ISA +12 °C
• Pressure altitude: 2 300 ft
• Indicated height on the altimeter 2 000 ft using the QFE from the airport, of 1 000 ft elevation set on the subscale.
• The altimeter experiences no instrument errors.
explanation: TRUE H = INDI H + TEMP CORR
